summary: Analyzes point, vertex, or primitive attributes and outputs a single-point POP containing statistics such as average, centroid, minimum, maximum, size, index of min/max, sum, RMS power, dimension, or P attribute values.

key_params.name: attrclass
key_params.note: Attribute class to analyze: point, vertex, or primitive

key_params.name: numgroupelements
key_params.note: Output the number of elements in the selected group

key_params.name: appendattrname
key_params.note: Append input attribute names to output statistic names

key_params.name: centroid
key_params.note: Output midpoint between minimum and maximum values

key_params.name: minindex
key_params.note: Output index of the minimum value

key_params.name: maxindex
key_params.note: Output index of the maximum value

key_params.name: numpointsvertsprims
key_params.note: Output point, vertex, and primitive counts

key_params.name: numprimsbatch
key_params.note: Output primitive and vertex counts per primitive type

key_params.name: pattrvals
key_params.note: Choose analyzed result to place in the output P attribute

key_concepts: Analyze POP reduces selected POP attributes into a single output point containing statistics such as average, bounds, size, indices, sums, counts, or dimension data.
Vector components are analyzed independently unless Combine Components first collapses each vector to a scalar.
Keeping the result in POPs is the fastest path; POP-to-CHOP or POP-to-DAT CPU readback is useful for inspection but adds delay or overhead.
common_gotchas: The result is a single point on the GPU; pulling it to CPU parameters is slower than keeping it in POPs.
When analyzing multiple attributes or * scope, output names are expanded with source attribute names.
Vector attributes are analyzed per component unless Combine Components is used intentionally.
